lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Belief in the angels
lessons.bigQuestion: If angels are with us all the time but we cannot see them, how should that change the way we behave?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe about the angels and how this belief affects daily life
successCriteria: All: describe three qualities of angels from the Qur'an and Sunnah
Most: match named angels to their roles
Some: explain how belief in angels shapes a Muslim's behaviour

keywords.def: angels: created by Allah from light to obey Him
the unseen: what we cannot see but believe in
the angel who brought revelation
the noble angels who write our deeds
revelation from Allah

hook.text: If angels are with us all the time but we cannot see them, how should that change the way we behave?
hook.a: Angels record our deeds (82:10-12), so a believer behaves well in private as in public.

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the believers as those who believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers (al-Baqarah 2:285). Belief in the angels is the second pillar of iman.

starter.q: How many pillars of iman are there?
What is tawhid?
starter.a: Believing Allah is One and worshipping Him alone
options: Believing Allah is One and worshipping Him alone

starter.q: Name the hadith that lists the pillars of iman.
What is shirk?

teach.heading: What are angels?
bullets: Created from light (Muslim)
Never disobey Allah (66:6)
Do not tire of worship (21:20)
Part of the unseen: believed, not seen
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. The Prophet ﷺ said angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what you have been told (Muslim). At-Tahrim 66:6: they do not disobey Allah in what He commands and do what they are commanded. Al-Anbiya 21:20: they glorify Him night and day and do not slacken. Al-Baqarah 2:3 praises those who believe in the unseen.

teach.heading: Angels and their roles
teach.note: Israfil is named in hadith, not the Qur'an; the Horn is in the Qur'an (39:68). Munkar and Nakir are named in a hadith reported by at-Tirmidhi.

teach.heading: Jibril and revelation
bullets: Brought the Qur'an to the Prophet ﷺ
Came at Hira with 'Iqra'
Seen in his true form with 600 wings
Came in human form in the hadith of Jibril
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his true form with six hundred wings (Bukhari, from Ibn Mas'ud). Never show pictures of angels; describe only what the texts say.

check.q: Which angel brought revelation to the prophets?
check.why: Jibril brought revelation (2:97). Mika'il is linked to rain and provision, Israfil to the Horn, Malik to Hell.

teach.heading: How it changes how we live
bullets: Every word written: guard the tongue (50:18)
Good company: angels love dhikr
Not alone: Allah's care through angels
Motivation to do good in private
teach.note: Qaf 50:18: not a word does he utter except that there is an observer ready. Ask pupils for one change they could make knowing this.

practice.q: Match: Jibril, Angel of Death, Kiraman Katibin, Malik to: record deeds, revelation, Hell, taking souls.
practice.a: Jibril: revelation. Angel of Death: taking souls. Kiraman Katibin: record deeds. Malik: Hell.
practice.model: I do the first: 'Jibril brought the Qur'an, so Jibril matches revelation (2:97).' Pupils do the rest on whiteboards.

practice.q: Angels were created from ...
practice.a: Light

practice.q: Which ayah says angels do not disobey Allah?
practice.a: At-Tahrim 66:6

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain how belief in the angels affects how a Muslim lives.'
independent.a: Point: they know deeds are recorded. Evidence: 82:10-12 or 50:18. Explain: e.g. careful speech and honesty in private. Link.
independent.model: Teacher models the Point and Evidence: 'Belief in angels makes a Muslim careful about what they say and do. Allah says noble angels record what we do (82:10-12).'

independent.q: Extend: why is belief in the unseen an important part of iman?
independent.a: Iman includes trusting Allah's word about things we cannot see; 2:3 praises those who believe in the unseen.

independent.q: Stretch: what is the difference between angels and humans in terms of free will?
independent.a: Angels always obey (66:6); humans have choice and are tested and held responsible.

exit.q: Which angel will blow the Horn?
Back to our ponder: how should unseen angels change our behaviour?
exit.a: Behave well in private and public because deeds and words are recorded.

lessons.homework: For one day, notice your words: write down three things you chose not to say because the angels record every word.
lessons.send: SEND: angel-role matching cards (words only, no images). EAL: key words with Arabic. Stretch: read 35:1 and 2:97-98 and summarise.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: angels and roles table and PEEL frame

pictures.alt: The night sky: the vast creation of Allah

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Belief in the revealed books
lessons.bigQuestion: If you had an instruction book from the person who made you, how carefully would you read it?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe about the books Allah revealed and why the Qur'an is special
successCriteria: All: match four books to the prophets who received them
Most: explain why the Qur'an is the final and protected book
Some: explain what 'muhaymin' (5:48) means for the earlier books
lessons.crossCurricular: History: how texts were preserved before printing, by memory and handwriting
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: love for and respect of the Qur'an

keywords.def: books revealed by Allah
the book given to Musa
the book given to Dawud
the book given to Isa
the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa
a guardian and judge over what came before

hook.text: If you had an instruction book from the person who made you, how carefully would you read it?
hook.a: Allah, our Creator, sent books of guidance; the Qur'an is the final one, protected by Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder (the Qur'an), and indeed, We will guard it' (al-Hijr 15:9). Belief in the books is the third pillar of iman.

starter.q: Angels were created from ...
Which angel brought revelation?
Which ayah says angels never disobey Allah?
What do the Kiraman Katibin do?

teach.heading: Books of guidance
bullets: Allah sent guidance to every people
Some books are named in the Qur'an
Muslims believe in all of them (2:285)
All taught tawhid
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Al-Baqarah 2:285: the believers believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. Muslims believe in the original books as Allah revealed them.

teach.heading: The named books
teach.note: An-Nisa 4:163: 'to Dawud We gave the Zabur'. Al-Ma'idah 5:46: Allah gave Isa the Injil. Al-A'la 87:18-19: the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa.

teach.heading: What happened to the earlier books?
bullets: Originals not preserved as revealed
Some words were changed by people (2:79)
The Qur'an confirms the truth in them
The Qur'an is the guardian over them (5:48)
teach.note: Al-Baqarah 2:79 warns those who write the book with their own hands then say 'this is from Allah'. Al-Ma'idah 5:48 calls the Qur'an a confirmation of what came before and a muhaymin over it. Teach respectfully: Muslims respect Jews and Christians as People of the Book.

check.q: Which book did Allah promise to protect Himself (15:9)?
check.why: 15:9 promises protection of the Qur'an (the Reminder). The earlier books were entrusted to their people and were not preserved as revealed.

teach.heading: How the Qur'an is protected
bullets: Memorised by huffadh in every age
Written in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime
Gathered under Abu Bakr
Standard copies sent out by Uthman
teach.note: After the Battle of Yamamah, Umar urged Abu Bakr to gather the Qur'an; Zayd ibn Thabit did it. Uthman later had copies made and sent to the main cities (both in Bukhari). Millions memorise it today, including children at TGA in hifdh.

practice.q: Match: Zabur, Injil, Tawrat, Suhuf to Musa, Isa, Dawud, Ibrahim.
practice.a: Zabur: Dawud. Injil: Isa. Tawrat: Musa. Suhuf: Ibrahim (and Musa).
practice.model: I do: 4:163 says 'to Dawud We gave the Zabur', so Zabur matches Dawud. Pupils match the rest on whiteboards.

practice.q: Who compiled the Qur'an into one copy for Abu Bakr?
practice.a: Zayd ibn Thabit

practice.q: What does 'muhaymin' mean?
practice.a: Guardian and judge over what came before

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain why Muslims believe the Qur'an is the final and protected book.'
independent.a: Point: Allah promised to protect it. Evidence: 15:9. Explain: memorisation, writing, compilation under Abu Bakr and Uthman. Link: so it is unchanged and final guidance.
independent.model: Teacher models: 'Point: Muslims believe the Qur'an has been protected from change. Evidence: Allah says "We will guard it" (15:9). Explain: ...'

independent.q: Extend: how should a Muslim treat the Qur'an in daily life?
independent.a: Recite it, understand it, act on it, handle it with respect, learn by heart (hifdh).

independent.q: Stretch: why do Muslims believe in the earlier books but follow the Qur'an?
independent.a: The earlier books were true in their original form but were not preserved; the Qur'an is the final, protected guidance and confirms the truth in them (5:48).

exit.q: Which book was given to Isa?
Back to our ponder: how carefully should we read Allah's book?
exit.a: With great care: recite, understand and act on it, because it is guidance from our Creator.

lessons.homework: Learn the five books and their prophets, and recite one surah you know to a family member with its meaning.
lessons.send: SEND: book and prophet matching cards. EAL: key words with Arabic. Stretch: read 5:44-48 in translation and note what each ayah says.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: books table and PEEL frame

An early handwritten copy of the Qur'an

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Belief in the messengers: their qualities and their miracles
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think Allah chose human beings, not angels, to be His messengers to people?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe about the messengers, their qualities and the miracles that supported them
successCriteria: All: define nabi and rasul and name the five ulul 'azm
Most: describe the qualities all messengers share
Some: explain why the Qur'an is the lasting miracle of Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: love and respect for every prophet

keywords.def: a messenger sent with a message to deliver
a prophet who receives revelation
a miracle Allah gave a prophet as proof
Allah's protection of prophets in conveying the message
the messengers of great determination

hook.text: Why do you think Allah chose human beings, not angels, to be His messengers to people?
hook.a: So people could see the message lived out by someone like them and follow a real example (18:110).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets' (al-Ahzab 33:40), and 'We have not sent you except to all people' (Saba 34:28).

starter.q: Which book was given to Dawud?
Which ayah promises the Qur'an's protection?
Who gathered the Qur'an under Abu Bakr?
What does 'muhaymin' mean?
starter.a: A guardian over what came before

teach.heading: Nabi and rasul
bullets: Allah sent messengers to every nation (16:36)
Many scholars: every rasul is a nabi
A rasul delivers a message to people
25 are named in the Qur'an
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Explain the common scholarly distinction carefully; scholars word it differently. An-Nisa 4:164: some messengers' stories are told, others are not.

teach.heading: Qualities of the messengers
bullets: Human, not divine (18:110)
Truthful and trustworthy
Conveyed the whole message
Protected from error in conveying it
teach.note: Al-Kahf 18:110: 'I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God.' 'Ismah: Allah protected them in conveying revelation and from major sins.

teach.heading: Miracles as proof
teach.note: Miracles matched what their people valued. The Qur'an challenges people to produce a surah like it (2:23). Never show pictures of prophets.

head: Prophet
Miracle (from the Qur'an)
Reference
rows: The fire became cool and safe
The staff and the parting of the sea
Healing and giving life by Allah's permission
The Qur'an: no one can produce its like

teach.heading: The Seal for all people
bullets: Ulul 'azm: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ
Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet (33:40)
His message is for all people (34:28)
teach.note: Al-Ahqaf 46:35 mentions the messengers of determination; they are commonly listed from 33:7 and 42:13. Saba 34:28 and al-A'raf 7:158: his message is for all mankind.

check.q: Why is the Qur'an called the 'lasting' miracle?
options: It can still be read and tested today
It was only for one generation
check.why: Earlier miracles were seen by those present; the Qur'an remains and its challenge (2:23) is still open.

practice.q: Ibrahim's miracle in 21:69 shows what about Allah?
practice.a: That Allah controls all things: fire burns only by His will, and He protects His messengers.
practice.model: I do: 1) The event: Ibrahim was thrown into a fire. 2) Allah said 'O fire, be coolness and safety' (21:69). 3) So fire has no power of its own; Allah controls it and protects His messengers.

practice.q: Name the five ulul 'azm.
practice.a: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ

practice.q: Which ayah calls Muhammad ﷺ the Seal of the Prophets?

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain why belief in the messengers is important for Muslims.'
independent.a: Point: they bring Allah's guidance. Evidence: 16:36 or 2:285. Explain: we learn tawhid and how to live; they are examples. Link.
independent.model: Teacher models the Point and Evidence: 'Belief in the messengers matters because they are how Allah's guidance reaches people. Allah sent a messenger to every nation (16:36).'

independent.q: Extend: why does it matter that messengers were human?
independent.a: People can follow a human example; it guards against worshipping them (18:110).

independent.q: Stretch: explain the challenge in 2:23 and why it is still a proof today.
independent.a: Allah challenges anyone in doubt to produce one surah like the Qur'an; it remains unmet, so the Qur'an still proves the message.

exit.q: Which prophet's sea was parted?
Back to our ponder: why humans, not angels?
exit.a: So people have a real example they can follow, someone like them (18:110).

lessons.homework: Choose one of the ulul 'azm and write a short fact file (no pictures of the prophet): his people, his book or miracle, and one lesson for today.
lessons.send: SEND: miracle and prophet matching cards. EAL: key words with Arabic. Stretch: compare 18:110 and 33:40.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: miracles table and PEEL frame

pictures.alt: The Red Sea, linked to the story of Musa
A page of the Qur'an, the lasting miracle

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: The Isra and Mi'raj
lessons.bigQuestion: After the hardest year of his life, what gift did the Prophet ﷺ receive, and why do you think it came then?
objectives: To understand the events of the Isra and Mi'raj and why salah is called its gift
successCriteria: All: sequence the main events of the night journey
Most: explain how the five prayers were given
Some: explain why Abu Bakr was called as-Siddiq
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: locating Makkah and Jerusalem (al-Quds) on a map of the Middle East
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: salah as the believer's meeting with Allah

keywords.def: the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem
the ascension through the heavens
the mosque in Jerusalem, the first qiblah
the lote tree of the furthest boundary
the one who always affirms the truth: Abu Bakr

hook.text: After the hardest year of his life, what gift did the Prophet ﷺ receive, and why do you think it came then?
hook.a: The Isra and Mi'raj, with the gift of the five daily prayers: comfort and honour after the Year of Sorrow.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs' (al-Isra 17:1).

starter.q: Who is the Seal of the Prophets?
What is a mu'jizah?
starter.a: A miracle given to a prophet as proof
options: A miracle given to a prophet

starter.q: Which two people died in the Year of Sorrow?
Which town rejected the Prophet ﷺ after the Year of Sorrow?

teach.heading: The Isra: Makkah to Jerusalem
bullets: One night, by Allah's power (17:1)
Carried by al-Buraq
Led the prophets in prayer at al-Aqsa
Al-Aqsa: the first qiblah
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Scholars differ on the exact date; it is commonly placed about a year before the Hijrah, after the Year of Sorrow and Ta'if. The Buraq is described in Bukhari and Muslim as a white animal smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey. No images.

teach.heading: The Mi'raj: through the heavens
teach.note: From the narrations in Bukhari and Muslim: Jibril accompanied him through the seven heavens, where he met prophets. An-Najm 53:13-18 mentions Sidrat al-Muntaha and the greatest signs.

teach.heading: The gift of salah
bullets: Fifty prayers were first prescribed
Musa advised asking for less
Reduced to five, reward of fifty
Given directly, without an intermediary on earth
teach.note: From the narrations in Bukhari and Muslim. The only pillar given in the heavens shows its importance. Ask: how should this change how we view our five prayers?

check.q: How many daily prayers were finally prescribed, and with what reward?
options: Five, with the reward of fifty
Fifty, with the reward of five
Three, with the reward of five
Seven, with the reward of seventy
check.why: Fifty were reduced to five after Musa's advice, with the reward of fifty kept (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: The test of belief
bullets: Quraysh mocked the journey
Some weak believers doubted
Abu Bakr: 'If he said it, it is true'
He was called as-Siddiq
teach.note: Seerah reports describe Abu Bakr's immediate belief, after which he was known as as-Siddiq. The Prophet ﷺ described Jerusalem to the Quraysh, which he had not visited before (Bukhari and Muslim mention Allah showing him Jerusalem when questioned).

practice.q: Put in order: reduced to five prayers; Makkah to al-Aqsa; met prophets in the heavens; led the prophets in prayer.
practice.a: Makkah to al-Aqsa; led the prophets in prayer; met prophets in the heavens; reduced to five prayers
practice.model: I do: the Isra comes first, from Makkah to al-Aqsa. There he led the prophets in prayer. Then the Mi'raj through the heavens, meeting prophets. Last, the prayers were given and reduced to five.

practice.q: Which ayah describes the Isra?
practice.a: Al-Isra 17:1

practice.q: Who advised asking for fewer prayers?
practice.a: Musa

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain why the Isra and Mi'raj is important to Muslims.'
independent.a: Point: it gave the five prayers. Evidence: 17:1; Bukhari and Muslim. Explain: comfort after hardship; honour of salah; link to al-Aqsa. Link.
independent.model: Teacher models: 'Point: the Isra and Mi'raj is important because it is when Allah gave the five daily prayers. Evidence: ...'

independent.q: Extend: why is al-Masjid al-Aqsa special to Muslims?
independent.a: The Isra was to it (17:1); the first qiblah; the prophets prayed there with him.

independent.q: Stretch: what can we learn from Abu Bakr's response?
independent.a: True iman trusts the Messenger's report even when the mind finds it amazing.

exit.q: Which prophet was in the seventh heaven?
Back to our ponder: what was the gift, and why then?
exit.a: The five prayers; it came after the Year of Sorrow as comfort and honour.

lessons.homework: Pray all five prayers on time for three days and write one sentence each day about how you prepared.
lessons.send: SEND: event cards with place pictures (no people). EAL: map with key places labelled. Stretch: read 53:1-18 in translation.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: night journey sequence and PEEL frame
Map of Makkah and Jerusalem (on screen)

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: The Hijrah: the plot, the cave and the journey
lessons.bigQuestion: Would you leave your home, your belongings and your city for your beliefs? What would make you do it?
objectives: To understand the events of the Hijrah and the planning and trust in Allah it shows
successCriteria: All: sequence the main events of the Hijrah
Most: describe the roles of Ali, Abu Bakr, Asma' and the guide
Some: explain how the Hijrah shows both planning and tawakkul
lessons.crossCurricular: History: chronology and the reasons for migration
lessons.smsc: Moral: loyalty, courage and sacrifice for what is right

keywords.def: migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE
the Muslims who migrated from Makkah
the cave where they hid for three nights
trusting Allah after doing your best
the Quraysh meeting house where they plotted

hook.text: Would you leave your home, your belongings and your city for your beliefs? What would make you do it?
hook.a: The Muhajirun did, for Allah: the Hijrah of 622 CE, so important that the Islamic calendar starts from it.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'If you do not help him, Allah already helped him when the disbelievers drove him out, the second of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us"' (at-Tawbah 9:40).

starter.q: Which ayah describes the Isra?
Who was called as-Siddiq?
What gift was given in the Mi'raj?
What were the two pledges before the Hijrah called?

teach.heading: Why leave Makkah?
bullets: Years of persecution in Makkah
Pledges of Aqabah with people of Yathrib
Muslims left quietly in small groups
Quraysh plotted at Dar an-Nadwah (8:30)
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Al-Anfal 8:30: 'when the disbelievers plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or evict you; they planned, and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners.'

teach.heading: The night of the plot
bullets: Ali slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed
Ali returned people's trusts
The Prophet ﷺ left safely
He met Abu Bakr; they went south to Thawr
teach.note: Seerah reports (Ibn Ishaq and others) describe Ali staying behind and returning the items people had left in the Prophet's ﷺ keeping: even his enemies trusted him. Going south when Madinah is north was a deliberate plan to mislead the searchers.

teach.heading: The cave and the journey
teach.note: Each person had a role. Abdullah ibn Urayqit was hired as the guide even though he was not Muslim: skill and trust mattered. Suraqah ibn Malik chased them but his horse's legs sank; he asked for safety (Bukhari).

timeline.label: Night 1
timeline.text: Leave Makkah, go south to Cave Thawr

timeline.label: Each day
timeline.text: Abdullah brings news; Asma' brings food; Amir's sheep hide tracks

timeline.label: Journey
timeline.text: Guide leads by a coastal route; Suraqah's horse sinks

teach.heading: Planning and trust
bullets: Plan: secret route, guide, supplies, helpers
Trust: 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us'
Both together: tie the camel and trust
The calendar begins at the Hijrah (1 AH)
teach.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab chose the Hijrah as the start of the Islamic calendar. Asma' bint Abi Bakr tore her waist-belt in two to tie the food, and was called Dhat an-Nitaqayn (Bukhari).

check.q: Which detail shows TRUST in Allah rather than planning?
options: 'Do not grieve; Allah is with us' (9:40)
check.why: 9:40 is trust when danger was at the cave's mouth. The others are planning: route, guide, supplies.

practice.q: Give the role of each: Ali, Asma', Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Abdullah ibn Urayqit.
practice.a: Ali: slept in the bed and returned trusts. Asma': brought food. Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr: brought news. Abdullah ibn Urayqit: the guide.
practice.model: I do: 'Ali slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed so the plotters thought he was still there, then returned people's trusts.' Pupils do the other three.

practice.q: Which cave did they hide in?
practice.a: Thawr

practice.q: In which year CE was the Hijrah?

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain how the Hijrah shows both careful planning and trust in Allah.'
independent.a: Point; evidence from the route, guide and helpers, and 9:40; explain both together; link to tawakkul.
independent.model: Teacher models the planning half: 'Point: the Hijrah was carefully planned. Evidence: they went south to Thawr although Madinah is north, and hired a skilled guide. Explain: ...'

independent.q: Extend: why did Umar choose the Hijrah to begin the calendar?
independent.a: It marked the start of the Muslim community and state in Madinah: a turning point.

independent.q: Stretch: what does returning the trusts tell us about the Prophet ﷺ?
independent.a: Even enemies trusted him (al-Amin); he kept his amanah while being persecuted.

exit.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the cave?
exit.a: 'Do not grieve; Allah is with us'
options: 'Do not grieve; Allah is with us'

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what made the Muhajirun leave?
exit.a: Faith in Allah and the need to practise Islam freely.

lessons.homework: Write a diary entry as Asma' bint Abi Bakr (no drawings of people) describing one day of the Hijrah.
lessons.send: SEND: role cards to match. EAL: map with route marked. Stretch: read 9:40 and explain 'second of two'.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: Hijrah roles and PEEL frame
Map of the route Makkah, Thawr, Quba, Madinah (on screen)

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Madinah: the mosque, the brotherhood and a new society
lessons.bigQuestion: If you arrived in a new town with nothing, what would you need most from the people there?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet ﷺ built a united society in Madinah
successCriteria: All: describe how Masjid an-Nabawi was built
Most: explain the brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar
Some: explain how the Charter of Madinah organised a mixed society
lessons.crossCurricular: History: how communities and rules for citizens develop
lessons.smsc: Social: welcoming newcomers and living together with others

keywords.def: the helpers: Muslims of Madinah
the brotherhood joining Muhajirun and Ansar
the Prophet's ﷺ mosque in Madinah
the Charter of Madinah: agreed rules for the city's communities
the community of believers

hook.text: If you arrived in a new town with nothing, what would you need most from the people there?
hook.a: Shelter, food, friendship and work: the Ansar gave the Muhajirun all of these through the brotherhood (mu'akhah).

islamicLink.text: Allah praises the Ansar: 'They love those who emigrated to them ... and give them preference over themselves, even though they are in need' (al-Hashr 59:9).

starter.q: In which cave did they hide?
Who was the guide on the Hijrah?
Which ayah records 'Allah is with us'?
What does Muhajirun mean?

teach.heading: The welcome and the mosque
bullets: The people of Madinah came out to welcome him
His camel knelt on land of two orphans
The land was bought, not taken
He carried bricks with the Companions
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Bukhari reports the camel kneeling, the land belonging to two orphan boys, and the Prophet ﷺ insisting on paying. He worked alongside the Companions carrying bricks (Bukhari). Ask: what does that tell us about his leadership?

teach.heading: More than a place of prayer
teach.note: Masjid an-Nabawi was the centre of community life.

teach.heading: The brotherhood (mu'akhah)
bullets: Each Muhajir paired with an Ansari
Ansar shared homes, work and wealth
Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' offered half his wealth
Abd ar-Rahman: 'Show me the market'
teach.note: Bukhari reports Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' offering half his wealth to Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, who thanked him and asked to be shown the market so he could trade. Lesson: generosity on one side, dignity and hard work on the other.

check.q: What did Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf's reply 'show me the market' show?
options: He did not need help at all
check.why: He thanked Sa'd and chose to earn for himself: dignity and hard work, not ingratitude.

teach.heading: The Charter of Madinah
bullets: A written agreement for all groups
Muslims and Jewish tribes as one community for defence
Each group kept its religion
Disputes referred to the Prophet ﷺ
teach.note: The Sahifah is recorded in the seerah (Ibn Ishaq) and early sources; historians discuss its exact text. Teach the main principles only: mutual defence, justice, freedom of religion for each group, and resolving disputes through the Prophet ﷺ.

practice.q: Explain why the Prophet ﷺ paid for the orphans' land.
practice.a: To be just: orphans' property must be protected; he did not use his position to take it.
practice.model: I do: 1) Who owned the land? Two orphans. 2) What does Islam teach about orphans' property? Protect it (4:10 warns against consuming it unjustly). 3) So he paid a fair price, showing justice.

practice.q: The Ansar were ...
practice.a: The Muslims of Madinah who helped
options: The Muslims of Madinah who helped

practice.q: Which ayah praises the Ansar for preferring others?

independent.q: In the portal response box write a PEEL paragraph: 'Explain how the Prophet ﷺ built a united society in Madinah.'
independent.a: Points: the mosque as a centre; the brotherhood; the Charter. Evidence: 59:9; Sa'd and Abd ar-Rahman. Explain unity and justice. Link.
independent.model: Teacher models the first point: 'Point: the Prophet ﷺ built the mosque first, as a centre for the whole community. Evidence: he helped carry bricks himself (Bukhari). Explain: ...'

independent.q: Extend: how could a school use the idea of mu'akhah for new pupils?
independent.a: Pair each new pupil with a buddy who helps them settle, shares notes and includes them.

independent.q: Stretch: why was a written charter important for a mixed city?
independent.a: Clear agreed rules protect everyone's rights, prevent conflict and make justice possible.

exit.q: Who offered half his wealth to Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf?
Back to our ponder: what did the Ansar give the newcomers?

lessons.homework: Do one act of welcome this week (for example helping a new neighbour or classmate) and write what you did and why.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards of the mosque, market, homes (no people). EAL: sentence frames. Stretch: research as-Suffah.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: Madinah society organiser and PEEL frame

pictures.alt: Mud bricks, like those of the first mosque

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: The Battle of Badr
lessons.bigQuestion: Can a small group ever beat a much bigger one? What would they need?
objectives: To understand the causes, events and importance of the Battle of Badr
successCriteria: All: give the date, place and numbers of the battle
Most: explain two reasons for the Muslim victory
Some: explain why Badr was a turning point
lessons.crossCurricular: History: causes, events and consequences of a significant battle
lessons.smsc: Moral: mercy to prisoners and the ethics of conflict

keywords.def: wells south-west of Madinah where the battle took place
a military expedition the Prophet ﷺ led himself
consultation
the Day of Criterion, a name for Badr (8:41)
prisoners of war

hook.text: Can a small group ever beat a much bigger one? What would they need?
hook.a: At Badr about 313 Muslims faced about 1,000: they had faith, unity, good counsel and Allah's help (3:123).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Allah had already given you victory at Badr while you were weak, so fear Allah that you may be grateful' (Al Imran 3:123).

starter.q: What is mu'akhah?
starter.a: The brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar
options: The brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar

starter.q: In which year was the Hijrah?
Who said 'show me the market'?
What is the Charter of Madinah?
starter.a: An agreement setting rules for the communities of Madinah

teach.heading: Causes
bullets: Muslims' homes and wealth taken in Makkah
Permission to fight given to the wronged (22:39)
Abu Sufyan's caravan returning from Syria
Quraysh sent an army of about 1,000
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Al-Hajj 22:39: permission is given to those who are fought against because they were wronged. The caravan changed route and escaped; Abu Jahl insisted on marching to Badr anyway.

teach.heading: The two sides
bullets: 17 Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE)
Muslims about 313, few horses
Quraysh about 1,000, well armed
teach.note: Bukhari reports the Muslims were about the number of Talut's army (310 and some). The bar chart shows the difference in size.

teach.heading: Why the Muslims won
bullets: Shura: al-Hubab's advice on the wells
Du'a: the Prophet ﷺ prayed through the night
Angels sent as help (8:9)
Unity, courage and faith
teach.note: Seerah reports al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir asking whether the position was revelation or strategy, then advising control of the wells; the Prophet ﷺ accepted. Al-Anfal 8:9: 'I will reinforce you with a thousand angels following one another.' Bukhari and Muslim describe the Prophet's ﷺ intense du'a.

check.q: What does al-Hubab's advice about the wells show about the Prophet's ﷺ leadership?
options: He consulted and accepted good advice
check.why: He asked for and accepted good counsel (shura) while relying on Allah; the other options are the opposite of what happened.

teach.heading: Results and lessons
bullets: About 70 Quraysh killed, including Abu Jahl
14 Muslims martyred
Prisoners treated well; some freed for teaching reading
Called the Day of Criterion (8:41)
teach.note: Seerah reports that literate prisoners could earn freedom by teaching ten Muslim children to read. Badr gave the Muslims confidence and showed Arabia that Islam would survive.

practice.q: Give two reasons for the Muslim victory, each with evidence.
practice.a: 1) Allah's help: 3:123 and 8:9. 2) Good leadership and shura: al-Hubab's advice on the wells. (Also du'a, unity, courage.)
practice.model: I do reason 1: 'One reason was Allah's help. Allah says He gave them victory at Badr while they were weak (3:123) and sent angels (8:9).' Pupils write reason 2.

practice.q: Badr took place in ...
practice.a: Ramadan, 2 AH

practice.q: How were literate prisoners able to gain freedom?
practice.a: By teaching Muslim children to read

independent.q: In the portal response box answer: 'Explain why the Battle of Badr was important for the early Muslims.' Use PEEL with two developed points.
independent.a: Points: proved Allah's support and raised confidence; established the Muslims as a power in Arabia; showed mercy to prisoners. Evidence 3:123, 8:41. Link.
independent.model: Teacher models point 1: 'Point: Badr showed the Muslims that Allah was with them. Evidence: "Allah had already given you victory at Badr while you were weak" (3:123). Explain: ...'

independent.q: Extend: what does the treatment of prisoners teach about Islam's ethics of war?
independent.a: Prisoners have rights: kindness, food and a route to freedom; war has rules.

independent.q: Stretch: why is Badr called the Day of Criterion?
independent.a: It distinguished truth from falsehood: the small believing army won by Allah's help (8:41).

exit.q: About how many Muslims fought at Badr?
Back to our ponder: what did the small group need?
exit.a: Faith, unity, good planning and consultation, and Allah's help.

lessons.homework: Write a short newspaper report (no pictures of people) on Badr: date, place, numbers, causes, result.
lessons.send: SEND: fact-file frame with numbers given. EAL: key word list. Stretch: read 8:5-19 in translation and find two lessons.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: causes and results organiser and PEEL frame
Map of Madinah, Badr and Makkah (on screen)

pictures.alt: A desert well, like the wells of Badr

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh and the sources of Islamic law
lessons.title: The sources of Shari’ah
objectives: Name the main sources of Islamic law
Explain ijma and qiyas simply
Explain the importance of following the Qur’an and Sunnah

keywords.def: the path of Islamic guidance and law from Allah
agreement of the scholars on a ruling
analogy: applying a ruling to a similar new case
scholarly effort to reach a ruling

teach.heading: What is Shari’ah?
bullets: “We made for each a way” (5:48)
The path to Allah’s pleasure
Covers worship, character and dealings
Aims to protect life, faith, mind, family and wealth
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Edexcel 2.7 passage: 5:48. Note that Shari’ah is far wider than punishments. Ask: what rules guide a school? Compare with the purpose of Shari’ah: a guide for good.

teach.heading: The Qur’an and Sunnah
bullets: The Qur’an is the first source
The Sunnah explains and applies it
“Obey Allah and obey the Messenger” (4:59)
Example: the Qur’an orders salah; the Sunnah shows how
teach.note: Also mention 59:7: ‘Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids, abstain.’ Ask: what would we lose without the Sunnah? Give the example of how to pray or how to perform Hajj.

teach.heading: Ijma: consensus
bullets: Agreement of the scholars of a time on a ruling
Example: the compilation of the Qur’an in one book
It cannot contradict the Qur’an and Sunnah
teach.note: Keep it simple. The Prophet ﷺ said his Ummah would not agree upon misguidance (reported in Ibn Majah and elsewhere with varying grading; do not quote it as a precise text). Better: explain that scholars across time have agreed on core matters like the five prayers.

teach.heading: Qiyas: analogy
bullets: Applying a known ruling to a new, similar case
Needs the same reason (illah)
Example: drugs and alcohol, as both intoxicate
teach.note: Use the standard example: alcohol is forbidden because it intoxicates; scholars apply the same reason to other intoxicants. Ask pupils to think of a modern situation where scholars need to reason (new technology). Note that ordinary pupils do not make rulings; we ask qualified scholars.

teach.heading: Following with humility
bullets: We ask qualified scholars
“Ask the people of knowledge if you do not know” (16:43)
Scholars may differ in minor matters
We keep respect and unity
teach.note: Mention the four schools in brief (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i, Hanbali) as ways scholars systematised law; we will revisit in Year 9. Teach adab: no insulting people who follow another valid opinion.

practice: List the four sources of Shari’ah.
Explain qiyas using the alcohol example.
Why do we need the Sunnah as well as the Qur’an?
independent: Create a diagram with the four sources and an example for each.
Write a paragraph on why qualified scholars are needed to answer fiqh questions.
Write a short Q and A: ‘Why does Islam have a law?’
exit: Name the first two sources of Shari’ah.
lessons.homework: Ask a trusted adult for one example of a ruling taken from the Qur’an and one from the Sunnah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: source cards to sort; stretch: discuss why a source hierarchy is needed.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh and the sources of Islamic law
lessons.title: Halal, haram and the five rulings
objectives: Define halal and haram
Explain the five categories of rulings with examples
Apply the categories to everyday situations

keywords.def: obligatory: rewarded for doing, sinful for leaving
recommended: rewarded for doing, not sinful for leaving
permitted: neither rewarded nor sinful
disliked: better to avoid
forbidden: sinful to do

starter: Name the four sources of Shari’ah.
Where in the Qur’an is Shari’ah mentioned?

teach.heading: Halal and haram
bullets: “Eat of what is lawful and good on the earth” (2:168)
Halal: permitted; haram: forbidden
Allah permits what is good and forbids what is harmful
Most things are halal unless prohibited
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The principle that the default is permissibility is accepted in matters of dealings and food. Edexcel passage 5:3 lists forbidden meats. Ask: why does Allah forbid? (Protect us from harm.)

teach.heading: The five rulings
bullets: Fard: five daily prayers
Mustahabb: extra voluntary prayers
Mubah: choosing which halal meal to eat
Makruh: wasting water
Haram: lying, stealing, riba, alcohol
teach.note: This is the Ahkam pentad in the Edexcel spec. Note that Hanafis also distinguish wajib from fard; keep to the five categories. Use a number line from ‘must do’ to ‘must not do’. Ask pupils to place examples.

teach.heading: The doubtful matters
bullets: “The halal is clear and the haram is clear”
Between them are doubtful matters
Whoever avoids them protects his religion
Narrated by an-Nu’man ibn Bashir (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Explain with a practical example: a food product with an unfamiliar ingredient; check the label or ask someone knowledgeable. Ask: how can we avoid over-worry as well as carelessness?

teach.heading: Applying the categories
bullets: Pray Fajr: fard
Read extra Qur’an: mustahabb
Choose a blue or red bag: mubah
Gossip: haram
teach.note: Run a sorting game with real-life scenarios. Discuss edge cases (e.g. a game that wastes time: makruh? haram?). Stress that we refer complex issues to scholars.

practice: Place these in the five categories: eating halal chicken; praying Dhuhr; backbiting; fasting an extra Monday; wasting food.
What should we do with doubtful matters?
independent: Create a ‘Five Rulings’ table with two examples each.
Write a paragraph on why Islam has categories of rulings.
Design a poster for food-label checking.
exit: Name the five categories of rulings.
lessons.homework: List five things you do daily and categorise them with explanations.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with colours; stretch: explain the wisdom of having a middle category (mubah).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Zakah: purifying wealth
lessons.bigQuestion: If everyone gave a small part of their savings every year to people in need, what would change in your town?
objectives: To understand what zakah is, who pays it, who receives it and why it purifies wealth
successCriteria: All: state the conditions for paying zakah
Most: calculate zakah and name the eight groups who receive it
Some: explain how zakah purifies both wealth and the giver
lessons.smsc: Social: responsibility for the poor in the community

keywords.def: obligatory charity: purification and growth
the minimum wealth before zakah is due
one full lunar year of holding the wealth
voluntary charity, given any time
a small charity paid before the Eid prayer at the end of Ramadan

hook.text: If everyone gave a small part of their savings every year to people in need, what would change in your town?
hook.a: Poverty would fall, debts would be eased, people would feel cared for: the aims of zakah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow' (at-Tawbah 9:103). Zakah is one of the five pillars of Islam.

starter.q: What does 59:9 praise the Ansar for?
What percentage is zakah on savings?
Name the five pillars of Islam.
Which battle took place in Ramadan 2 AH?

teach.heading: What is zakah?
bullets: Meaning: purification and growth
A pillar of Islam, often paired with salah (2:43)
Wealth belongs to Allah; we are trustees
A right of the poor, not a favour
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Al-Baqarah 2:43: establish prayer and give zakah. 9:103: it purifies. Contrast with sadaqah, which is voluntary.

teach.heading: Who pays, on what?
bullets: A Muslim with wealth above the nisab
Held for one lunar year (hawl)
Cash, gold, silver, business stock: 2.5%
Crops and livestock have their own rules
teach.note: The nisab is linked to 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver; families check today's value with their masjid. Crops are paid at harvest at different rates. Keep it simple: Year 8 focus is savings.

model.problem: Yahya has held £5,200 in savings, above the nisab, for one lunar year. How much zakah does he pay?

teach.heading: Who receives zakah? (9:60)
teach.note: At-Tawbah 9:60 names eight groups. Zakah cannot be given to one's own parents or children (whom one must support anyway), as scholars explain.

items: Those whose hearts are being brought together

teach.heading: Why zakah purifies
bullets: Purifies wealth: the poor's share removed
Purifies the heart from greed
Builds love between rich and poor
Wealth grows with barakah
teach.note: Ask: how could giving away money make wealth grow? (Barakah, a fairer society, and reward.)

check.q: Which of these can receive zakah according to 9:60?
check.why: Debtors are one of the eight groups. Zakah is for those named in 9:60, not the rich.

practice.q: Calculate the zakah on £3,600 of savings held above the nisab for a lunar year.
Zakah or sadaqah: giving £5 to a charity box on any day you choose.
practice.a: Sadaqah

practice.q: What is the hawl?
practice.a: One lunar year of holding the wealth

independent.q: Zakah problems (pupil PDF): a) £8,000 b) £12,400 c) £1,600 savings held a lunar year, all above the nisab. Then write two sentences in the portal response box on how zakah helps society.
independent.a: a) £200 b) £310 c) £40. Helps the poor and debtors, reduces inequality, builds unity.
independent.model: Teacher works a) first: 10% of £8,000 = £800; quarter of £800 = £200.

independent.q: Extend: explain the difference between zakah, sadaqah and zakat al-fitr.
independent.a: Zakah: obligatory 2.5% yearly above the nisab. Sadaqah: voluntary, any time. Zakat al-fitr: small fixed charity before the Eid prayer.

independent.q: Stretch: how does zakah show that wealth is a trust from Allah?
independent.a: The owner must give the share Allah set to those He named; wealth is held for Allah, not owned absolutely.

exit.q: Which surah lists the eight groups of zakah?
Back to our ponder: what would change in your town?
exit.a: Less poverty and debt, more care and unity.

lessons.homework: Ask at home or at your masjid what today's nisab value is (in gold or silver) and write how it was worked out.
lessons.send: SEND: calculator allowed; 10% then quarter method card. EAL: picture cards for the eight groups. Stretch: research how zakah on crops is calculated.

pictures.alt: A wheat harvest: crops have their own zakah

lessons.title: Hadith: the believers are like one body
objectives: Explain the hadith of the body and the hadith on brotherhood
Link them to Muslim unity and compassion
Apply them to school and community

keywords.def: brotherhood and sisterhood in faith
mercy and compassion
the global Muslim community
mutual mercy

starter: Name one category of zakah recipient.
Why did the Ansar welcome the Muhajirun?

teach.heading: One body
bullets: “The believers in their mutual love and mercy are like one body”
“When one part is in pain, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever”
Narrated by an-Nu’man ibn Bashir (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Ask: when you stub a toe, who feels it? The whole person. Likewise, we feel for others’ pain. Link to current events: Muslims who suffer in different parts of the world. Encourage action: du’a, giving, awareness.

teach.heading: A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim
bullets: “He does not wrong him or hand him over”
Allah helps the one who helps his brother
Narrated by Ibn Umar (Bukhari, Muslim)
Qur’an: “The believers are but brothers” (49:10)
teach.note: Full hadith: a Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he does not wrong him or abandon him. Whoever fulfils his brother’s need, Allah fulfils his need; whoever removes a hardship, Allah removes a hardship from him on the Day of Judgment. Ask pupils to give practical examples at school.

teach.heading: How to live it
bullets: Greet with salam
Help in need
Forgive and settle disputes (49:9-10)
Pray for each other
teach.note: Role play: two pupils disagree about a game; one applies 49:10. Show the steps of making peace: listen, apologise, forgive, restore. Link to Y6 love for your brother what you love for yourself.

teach.heading: Brotherhood beyond differences
bullets: Muslims come from many races and nations
“The most noble of you is the one with most taqwa” (49:13)
Racism and pride are rejected
teach.note: Edexcel 2.8 passage 49:11-13. Mention the Prophet’s farewell sermon later (Y9). Ask: what steps can a school take to include everyone?

practice: Explain the ‘one body’ hadith in your own words.
Give three ways to help a classmate who is struggling.
independent: Write a short captioned scene script showing the ‘one body’ hadith in a school setting.
Write a paragraph: ‘What does brotherhood mean for the Ummah today?’
Plan a small act of service you will do this week and explain the hadith behind it.
exit: What does ‘one body’ mean in the hadith?
Give one rule of brotherhood from the hadith of Ibn Umar.
lessons.homework: Do one act of help for someone at home and write what you learned.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scene script template; stretch: link the hadith to the story of the Ansar and Muhajirun.

lessons.title: Akhlaq: truthfulness and avoiding lies
objectives: Explain the hadith on truthfulness and lying
State the signs of hypocrisy in the hadith
Apply honesty to school and online life

keywords.def: truthfulness
lying
hypocrisy: showing faith outwardly while hiding disbelief or insincerity
trust

starter: Name a good manner shown to a neighbour.

teach.heading: Truthfulness leads to Paradise
bullets: “Truthfulness leads to righteousness”
“Righteousness leads to Paradise”
“A man keeps being truthful until he is written truthful with Allah”
Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The same hadith warns that lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; a man keeps lying until he is written as a liar with Allah. Ask: how does one small lie lead to another? Use a school example.

teach.heading: Signs of the hypocrite
bullets: When he speaks, he lies
When he promises, he breaks it
When trusted, he betrays
Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (Bukhari, Muslim)
teach.note: Explain nifaq (hypocrisy in action) and that this hadith warns of traits to avoid; it does not mean we label individuals. Ask: which of the three traits do people find hardest to avoid? Discuss how to repair broken trust.

teach.heading: Honesty in modern life
bullets: Do not cheat in exams
Do not share fake news or false quotes
Keep promises to friends and family
Admit mistakes and say sorry
teach.note: Link to hadith checking and online speech. The Prophet ﷺ taught that it is enough lying for a person to speak about everything he hears (Muslim, Abu Hurayrah). Ask: what should you do before forwarding a message?

teach.heading: Building a truthful character
bullets: Keep the company of the truthful (9:119)
Remember Allah is watching
Speak good or keep silent
Make du’a for a truthful tongue
teach.note: Qur’an 9:119: ‘O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful.’ Pupils set personal honesty goals and share. Close with revision of the half-term and a short quiz.

practice: Complete the chain: truthfulness leads to ______ which leads to ______.
Give an example of breaking a promise and how to repair it.
Why is sharing unchecked news a form of lying?
independent: Write a short story where a pupil tells the truth when it is hard.
Make a poster of the three signs of hypocrisy with positive opposites.
Write a plan to build honesty in your daily life.
exit: State the three signs of hypocrisy from the hadith.
lessons.homework: Write a short apology or promise-repair letter for a real situation, or keep an honesty log for three days.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with pictures; stretch: discuss when honesty is difficult and how to be both truthful and kind.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Iman and the sources of Shari'ah
lessons.title: Lessons from the Seerah: from Makkah to Badr
lessons.bigQuestion: Which moment from Makkah to Badr teaches you the most about how to live today, and why?
objectives: To understand the key lessons the Seerah from Makkah to Badr teaches about faith, character and leadership
successCriteria: All: link four events to the lesson each teaches
Most: support each lesson with evidence
Some: write a balanced answer on which lesson matters most today
lessons.crossCurricular: English (Year 8 non-fiction): writing a balanced argument with evidence
lessons.smsc: Moral: applying the Prophet's ﷺ example to our own choices

keywords.def: patience and steadfastness
trusting Allah after doing your best
preferring others over yourself (59:9)
consultation
an excellent example (33:21)

hook.text: Which moment from Makkah to Badr teaches you the most about how to live today, and why?
hook.a: Any well-argued answer: e.g. the cave (trust), the brotherhood (generosity) or Badr (consultation).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example, for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often' (al-Ahzab 33:21).

starter.q: Which ayah says Allah gave victory at Badr while you were weak?
Which Companion advised on the wells at Badr?
Who slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed on the night of the Hijrah?
What is ithar?

teach.heading: Four events, four lessons
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Build the table together; pupils suggest the lesson before you reveal it.

head: Event
Lesson
Evidence
rows: Salah is a gift; ease after hardship

teach.heading: Sort: which lesson?
teach.note: Discuss each card; some could fit two columns, which is good for discussion.

cards: A. 'Do not grieve; Allah is with us'
B. Returning the trusts of enemies
D. Abu Bakr believing the night journey
E. Paying the orphans for the land
F. Carrying bricks with the Companions

teach.heading: Living the lessons today
bullets: Hard times: sabr and du'a
Big decisions: plan, consult, trust
New people: welcome and share
Responsibility: serve, do not just command
teach.note: Ask for a real situation for each (exams, moving house, a new pupil, being a team captain).

check.q: A team captain helps set up the hall instead of only giving orders. Which Seerah moment does this follow?
check.why: He ﷺ carried bricks with the Companions: a leader who serves. The others teach trust and patience.

teach.heading: Writing a balanced answer
bullets: State your view
Give a reason with evidence
Consider another view
Reach a justified conclusion
teach.note: This is the structure pupils will use for 12-mark 'assess this statement' answers in Years 10 and 11.

practice.q: Statement: 'The Hijrah teaches more than Badr.' Write the first two sentences of a balanced answer.
practice.a: For example: 'Some would agree, because the Hijrah shows planning and tawakkul together (9:40). However, Badr teaches consultation and reliance on Allah when outnumbered (3:123).'
practice.model: I do: 'Some would agree, because the Hijrah shows careful planning and trust in Allah together: "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us" (9:40). However, others would argue that ...'

practice.q: Which event best teaches ithar?
practice.a: The brotherhood (59:9)

independent.q: In the portal response box: 'The most important lesson from the Seerah for young Muslims today is patience.' Write a balanced answer of two paragraphs and a conclusion.
independent.a: View with evidence (Makkah, Ta'if, 9:40); another view (e.g. consultation at Badr, generosity of the Ansar); justified conclusion.
independent.model: Teacher models the first paragraph: 'Some would agree, because the Prophet ﷺ was patient through years of persecution in Makkah ... For example, in the cave he said ... (9:40). This shows ...'

independent.q: Extend: add a sentence linking your conclusion to 33:21.
independent.a: The Prophet ﷺ is the excellent example in every one of these qualities, so ...

independent.q: Stretch: which event surprised you most this unit and why?
independent.a: Personal, reasoned answer.

exit.q: Which ayah calls the Prophet ﷺ an excellent example?
Back to our ponder: which moment teaches you most, and why?

lessons.homework: Choose one lesson from the Seerah and put it into practice this week; write what you did in four sentences.
lessons.send: SEND: event and lesson cards to match. EAL: balanced-answer frame with connectives (however, on the other hand). Stretch: use three events in your answer.
resources: Pupil PDF worksheet: events and lessons table and balanced-answer frame

lessons.bigQuestion: Which pillar of iman or Seerah event from this unit means the most to you personally, and why?

successCriteria: All: complete the unit quiz
Most: correct mistakes and explain the right answers
Some: write a thoughtful reflection linking belief and action

islamicLink.text: Allah taught: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge' (Ta Ha 20:114). رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا

starter.q: Zakah on £2,400 above the nisab?
Which book was given to Musa?
Which prophet was in the sixth heaven?

teach.heading: Quiz rules
bullets: Bismillah and du'a first
Read every question twice
Answer every question
Your own work, no notes
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah and Rabbi zidni 'ilma. Run the quiz as a Teams Form (independent task, 14 minutes).

teach.heading: Going through answers
bullets: Mark in a different colour
Write why the right answer is right
Note topics to revisit
teach.note: Share Forms results; reteach the two most-missed questions.

check.q: Re-check: which ayah lists the eight groups who receive zakah?
check.why: 9:60 lists the recipients. 9:40 is the cave, 3:123 Badr, 17:1 the Isra.

teach.heading: Written reflection
bullets: Choose one belief or event
What it teaches
How it changes one thing you do
A du'a or intention
teach.note: Reflection in the portal response box. Spring 2: hadith and akhlaq (the believers like one body; truthfulness).

practice.q: Practice question: 'Give two roles of angels with evidence.'
practice.a: Jibril brings revelation (2:97); the Kiraman Katibin record deeds (82:10-12); the Angel of Death takes souls (32:11).
practice.model: I do: 'One role is bringing revelation: Jibril brought the Qur'an (2:97).'

independent.q: Unit quiz (Teams Forms, 12 questions): 1) Angels are created from? 2) Role of Jibril? 3) Book given to Dawud? 4) Ayah promising the Qur'an's protection? 5) Name the ulul 'azm. 6) Ayah of the Isra? 7) How many prayers were finally given? 8) Cave of the Hijrah? 9) Ayah 'Allah is with us'? 10) What is mu'akhah? 11) Date of Badr? 12) Zakah on £4,800 above the nisab?
independent.a: 1) Light 2) Brings revelation 3) Zabur 4) 15:9 5) Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ 6) 17:1 7) Five 8) Thawr 9) 9:40 10) Brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar 11) 17 Ramadan 2 AH 12) £120
independent.model: Teacher answers a sample question aloud (not in the quiz): 'Who blows the Horn? Israfil, as described in hadith; the Horn is mentioned in 39:68.'

independent.q: Reflection in the portal response box: 'One belief or event from this unit that changes how I live.' Start: 'This half term I learnt ...'
independent.a: Names the belief or event, what it teaches, one concrete change, and an intention.

exit.q: Write your target for Spring 2 in the chat.
Back to our ponder: which belief or event means most to you?

lessons.homework: Correct every quiz mistake with the reason, and revise the topic you scored lowest on.
lessons.send: SEND: quiz read aloud, extra time, options for recall questions. EAL: glossary allowed. Stretch: reflection must include an ayah with reference.
resources: Teams Forms unit quiz (12 questions, in the independent section)
Pupil PDF: corrections and reflection sheet
